# E041 -- Stella Artois Brand Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Company:** Stella Artois (AB InBev)
- **Industry:** Beer / Beverage
- **Year:** 2019
- **Source file:** stella-artois-pdf.pdf
- **Pages:** 79
- **Language:** EN
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 3-5, 6-7, 8-13, 16-20

## Brand Strategy
- Titled "Brand Guidelines 2019" -- comprehensive identity system document
- Emphasis on "premium quality and timeless character" that has made Stella Artois globally famous
- Design strategy translates brand ideal into tangible, usable design language
- "Took inspiration from our past to craft a design strategy that moves us into the future"
- Deep heritage storytelling: origins traced to 1366 Leuven brewing tradition, Den Hoorn brewery, Sebastian Artois (1708)
- "Stella" = star in Latin, originally a Christmas gift batch to the people of Leuven
- Nine-Step Pouring Ritual is a significant brand element (marketing initiative from 1997)
- TOC: Brand History, Design Strategy, Kit-of-Parts, Logos, Color, Typography, Pattern, Photography, Contacts

## Logo
- **Full Color Cartouche** -- packaging and iconic chalice ONLY; Global Brand Team permission required for other uses
- **Red Cartouche** -- primary logo; simplified single-color version for bolder, more contemporary look; "our signature"
  - White version for colored backgrounds; black version for cost/printing limitations
  - Approved uses: comms, social, experiential, trade, merchandise, LTO/heritage, high-end venues, pack
- **Outlined Cartouche** -- secondary mark
- **Horizontal Wordmark** -- secondary mark
- **Circular Wordmark** -- secondary mark
- **Outlined Stage** -- secondary mark
- **Red Stage** -- secondary mark
- **Heritage Marks** -- for heritage/LTO applications
- Logo evolution documented from 1926 to present across logo, bottle, and chalice designs

## Typography
- **Apercu Pro** -- primary font
- Full weight/style details likely on later pages (pp.82-90 per TOC)

- Color section referenced in TOC (p.82) and Kit-of-Parts overview

- **Illustration** -- included as a brand element in the kit-of-parts

## Applications
- Packaging (full color cartouche exclusive)

## Tone of Voice
- Heritage-driven storytelling: rich, detailed historical narrative woven throughout
- Premium positioning language: "premium quality", "timeless character", "proudly displayed"
- Invitational but authoritative: "So next time you see a bottle of Stella Artois, take note..."

## Outliers
- **79-page document** is very comprehensive for a single beer brand
- Cartouche-based logo system with strict packaging-only rules for full-color version is unusual
- Extensive historical timeline from 1366 to present -- one of the deepest heritage narratives encountered
- Kit-of-Parts framework explicitly includes illustration and pattern as core brand elements alongside standard assets
- Chalice design evolution tracked separately from logo and bottle -- the glass vessel is a brand asset
- Nine-Step Pouring Ritual elevated to brand-defining element

## Quality Score
- **4/5** -- Comprehensive and well-structured with deep heritage integration; strong logo hierarchy and kit-of-parts framework; dock one point because color values and typography details were not in sampled pages (appear later in the 79-page document)
